text.text: Your billing desk in one place. Log hours under Time entries, turn Unbilled time into Invoices, and watch Overdue and Part paid invoices so nothing slips. Tracking only; client trust accounting stays in your accounting system.
Clients pay invoices they understand. Clear, prompt time entries are the base of every invoice and the best defense against fee disputes.
Enter time the same day, in tenths of an hour (6 minutes).
One task per entry. "Reviewed lease amendments and called client" is two entries.
Describe the work and its purpose in words a client understands.
Pick the right matter. Time on the wrong matter is the most common billing error.
Record non-billable time too, with a note. It shows where effort goes.

Filing fees, courier charges, transcripts and expert fees are recorded as expenses on the matter the day they are paid, with the receipt. Expenses left off a bill are rarely recovered later, and clients accept them more readily when they arrive with the month they belong to.

When the client disputes a bill

Ask what they disagree with, in detail. The attorney reviews the entries, often offers a partial write-down, and confirms the agreement in writing. Many disputes come from surprises; the budget call during pre-bills prevents them.
Odalys Fontaine's formation invoice is five days overdue and her follow-up invoice is part paid. The collections owner emails a reminder today and calls next Tuesday if there is no reply.
Write the date, who you spoke to and what was promised on the invoice's page after every contact. When the attorney takes over at 31 days, they need the history in one place, not in someone's inbox.

text.text: Set the review for the same morning each month and keep it short. The value is in doing it every month, not in a long meeting.
Three lines to the partners: what went well, what slipped, one change for next month. Keep notes on this page under a heading for each month so trends are easy to see.

This month 92 percent of recorded hours were billed and 81 percent of billed work was collected. The contractor dispute had the most written down; the attorney will propose a revised budget to the client.

The billing office of a small firm: every hour recorded, which hours are on a draft invoice, which invoices are out, what clients still owe, and what was paid from trust. Your accounting system and trust ledger remain the books of record; this is the working desk.

: standard rate, budget, hours logged, unbilled hours, value logged and budget left.

text.text: Money in trust belongs to the client until it is earned and invoiced. Pay an invoice from trust only after the invoice is sent, record it in
, and update the client's trust balance from the ledger. Never move trust money to pay firm expenses or another client's bill.
